selected.title: The answer arrives with its sources
selected.texas_link: UTMB runs hospitals on four campuses and more than 100 clinics across Southeast Texas, and its clinicians ask an AI tool questions from within the patient record.

movement.action: announced OpenEvidence inside its electronic health record
movement.object: clinician questions answered with citations in the patient record

selected.why_today: UTMB announced the integration on September 22nd and the Docket recorded it with a fetched primary release, so it is the freshest clinic movement not covered by the recent films.
selected.consequence: UTMB says more than half of its clinicians actively use the tool for clinical decision support, so a question typed inside the chart now returns an answer with citations.
selected.application_change: A UTMB clinician signs in with their usual UTMB credentials and asks a clinical question from within the electronic health record, and the answer comes back with citations to medical literature and guidelines.
selected.counter_image: The release publishes no accuracy measure and no patient-care result, so the citations show where an answer says it came from and do not show that it is right.
selected.earned_take: A question now goes into UTMB's chart and comes back with citations, and the release publishes no measure of whether those answers are right.

agency.next_step: UTMB says it will keep evaluating utilization, clinician experience and how evidence is delivered at the point of care.
agency.who_can_act: UTMB administration decides. The UT System Board of Regents meets in public and takes testimony on agenda topics.

filmability.viewer_question: When a Galveston clinician asks an AI a medical question inside the patient record, what comes back, and what has UTMB not measured?
filmability.opening_action: An explanatory diagram labelled Illustration. A clinician's enterprise credential opens the edge of the chart, and a question leaves the record and returns with a stack of citation cards. No vendor interface, no face, no patient.
filmability.mechanism: Input: sign-in with UTMB credentials, then a natural-language question. Transformation: the question is authenticated and answered with citations to literature, guidelines and other sources. Result: citations attached to the return. Limit: no accuracy or patient-care measure is published.
filmability.human_consequence: UTMB states more than half of its clinicians use the tool for clinical decision support. No source shows any patient's care changed. The decision stays with the clinician and the outcome is unknown.
filmability.source_limit: UTMB's own release is the only primary source for the integration, and the adoption share is a self-report with no denominator. It publishes no accuracy, outcome or independent evaluation. The Abridge movement is vendor-only and the UT System page names Qualified Health, not Abridge. Whether clinician-facing AI falls under Sec. 183.005 or H.B. 149 is not answered by any source.
three_key_images: Credential at the record boundary (diagram, Illustration)
Question out, cited sources back (diagram, Illustration). The cards show source types only.
The unmeasured card (native text, sourced): accuracy and patient care are not published, with the release's will-continue-evaluating sentence.

action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of the relationship UTMB describes. It does not show UTMB's real screen, a vendor interface, any answer's content, a clinician or a patient. Authored fresh for this edition.
action_support.relationship: UTMB says answers include citations to medical literature, clinical guidelines and other authoritative sources. Disclosed relationship between a question and its source types, with no answer content.

action_support.pictured_action: The returned answer reaches a clinician-decision node while an open tag reads accuracy and patient care not published.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of the relationship UTMB describes. It does not show UTMB's real screen, a vendor interface, any answer's content, a clinician or a patient. Authored fresh for this edition.
action_support.relationship: UTMB says more than half of its clinicians use the tool for clinical decision support and publishes no accuracy or care measure. Disclosed conceptual card of the stated use and the unmeasured limit.

visual_stakes.affected_group: UTMB clinicians who use the tool and the patients whose records it sits inside. No patient-level data is in any source.
visual_stakes.physical_subject: a clinician's question inside the chart and the cited answer that returns
visual_stakes.visible_change: a question leaves the record and returns with citations attached
visual_stakes.consequence: UTMB reports more than half its clinicians actively use the tool for clinical decision support. No outcome is published.
visual_stakes.opening_question: What comes back when a clinician asks a medical question inside the record?
visual_stakes.answer: Answers with citations, per UTMB. The release publishes no accuracy check.
